adversarial_probes.description: verifyEffectGrants: grant with validUntil=500, now=1000 (expired) on effect_resource → deny. Not covered by existing tests which use grants without validUntil.
adversarial_probes.detail: isEffective gate correctly rejects expired grant. verifyEffectGrants returns {ok:false, missingResourceId:EP_1}. Also verified future grant (validUntil=2000, now=1000) passes. Gateway (resolveFor) returns {denied:true, reason:'no_effect_grant'} on expired effect grant even when normal record grant is valid. Reverted.

adversarial_probes.description: Declare TWO effects (ep-1 integration_endpoint, ep-2 messaging_channel), grant only on ep-1 → all-or-nothing deny. verifyEffectGrants returns missingResourceId=EP_2 (second declaration fails).
adversarial_probes.detail: verifyEffectGrants short-circuits at first uncovered declaration (ep-2), returns {ok:false, missingResourceId:EP_2}. Gateway denies with no_effect_grant even though record grant is fully covering. Holding both grants permits. Three cases verified. Reverted.

adversarial_probes.description: op='invoke', deps.effects present (EffectSource wired), invokeCtx=undefined (5th arg omitted) → pure-floor. This is the semantic the reviewer flagged in nit R-1: 'invokeCtx absent + EffectSource present = treated as pure-compute'.
adversarial_probes.verdict: pass (nit R-1 comment not yet in code but behaviour is correct per NF-2/AC-8 spec latitude)
adversarial_probes.detail: With invokeCtx absent, grant-resolver.ts line 406 defaults declares=[] → classifyTool([])={pure:true} → step 3.5 exits without effect verification → resolveFor returns {denied:false}. This is DISTINCT from NF-2 backward compat (absent EffectSource port): here EffectSource IS wired but invokeCtx is absent — the tool passes as pure-compute. Contrast: invokeCtx present with null declares → fail-closed (denied:true, reason:'no_effect_grant'). The trust boundary (composition root responsibility to always supply invokeCtx when invoking mcp_tool) is confirmed by this probe. Nit R-1 comment not present in code — flagged in friction. Reverted.

adversarial_probes.description: EffectSource.getEffect throws an exception → verify fail-closed (not crash-open, not allow). Mirrors probe-e from T-0033.
adversarial_probes.verdict: pass (same pattern as T-0033 ClassificationSource; exception propagates = deny at composition root)
adversarial_probes.detail: verifyEffectGrants does NOT catch EffectSource exceptions — they propagate. resolveFor similarly propagates (rejects). Security is preserved: no exception case resolves to permit. The fail-closed mode is fail-by-crash (exception) rather than fail-closed-to-deny (clean {denied:true} result), same as T-0033 probe-e. This is acceptable: the composition root must catch and treat as deny. Not an AC violation. Reverted.

adversarial_probes.description: Grant with resourceType='messaging' (not 'effect_resource'), same resourceId and scope → excluded from coverage check. The verifyEffectGrants step 4 requires resourceType==='effect_resource'.
adversarial_probes.detail: A grant with resourceType='messaging' on EP_1 does not cover the effect_resource declaration for EP_1 — verifyEffectGrants returns {ok:false}. When both wrong-type and correct-type grants are present, the correct one wins and result is {ok:true}. Gateway with only wrong-type grant returns {denied:true, reason:'no_effect_grant'}. Confirms no type-confusion bypass possible. Reverted.

failures.test: ci/checks/db/schema.test.ts :: FF-ACT :: zero ACT_* tables exist
failures.detail: schema.test.ts counts ALL information_schema.tables WHERE table_name LIKE 'act\_%' without schema filter. Our isolated compose project (choros-t0034-test) starts Flowable alongside Postgres, which creates 56 ACT_* tables in the 'flowable' schema. The test expects 0. This test was NOT modified in T-0034 build commit (8785f39 --stat shows schema.test.ts not listed); it is a pre-existing test that only passes when Flowable is NOT co-started. In the standard CI (GitHub Actions) the Postgres service is started separately without Flowable. This is a tester-isolation tooling-gap (correct fix: start only the postgres service, not the full compose stack, for the fitness:db job — or add a schema filter to the test).

R-1.probe_confirmation: Probe (c) confirms the actual behaviour: invokeCtx absent with EffectSource wired treats declares=[] (pure-compute, permitted). This is correct per spec latitude (ADR §4.4 option 2: 'no signature break for callers that omit it'), but the trust boundary comment requested by the reviewer is not yet present. Not a blocking defect — spec grants latitude. Recommend addressing before T-0043 imports the seam.
